categories.regulator_note: No regulator approves or must be notified before a grain elevator, cooperative, merchant or trader replaces its grain accounting ERP or CTRM. The constraints sit around the core, not on the switch itself. (1) US Warehouse Act (7 CFR 735): electronic warehouse receipts can only be issued through a central filing system run by a provider that has signed a provider agreement with USDA FSA. That approval covers the third-party EWR provider, not the warehouse's own accounting system. The new system still has to produce records that USDA or state warehouse examiners accept (https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-2018-title7-vol7/xml/CFR-2018-title7-vol7-part735.xml). (2) Listed merchants carry SOX internal-control risk during ERP cutovers. CHS reported material weaknesses in IT general controls tied to its new ERP in FY2018 (CHS FY2019 10-K). ADM's FY2024 10-K reports a material weakness and says it made no ERP deployments that year. (3) Public commodity agencies (USDA AMS/FSA WBSCM, Perum Bulog, India FCI) follow their own government procurement and audit rules, not a sector regulator's approval. I found no jurisdiction among US, EU, UK, SG, IN, ID, VN, MY, TH, PH or AU that requires prior regulator sign-off for a private trader's core-system replacement.

workflows.workflow: Inbound receiving: scale tickets, sampling and grading
workflows.description: Trucks are weighed gross and tare at the elevator or receival site. Loads are probed and graded for moisture, test weight, foreign material and damage. The scale ticket, grade factors and discounts are keyed into the grain accounting receiving screen, which becomes the record for inventory, settlement and warehouse receipts.

Hedge on futures exchanges, reconcile the daily position report against broker statements, and report P&L and risk to management. At traders this runs in a CTRM. At elevators it is often a grain-accounting position report plus spreadsheets, which can be overlaid without replacing the core.

categories.regulator_note: No aviation regulator (FAA/DOT, EASA/national CAAs, UK CAA, CAAS, DGCA, Kemenhub, CAAV, CAAM, CAAT, CAB, CASA) approves an airline's choice or swap of PSS. Vendor selection and cutover are commercial decisions; Air India, Malaysia Airlines, Garuda and others announced migrations without regulatory sign-off. The constraint is the border-data interfaces the PSS/DCS feeds. Under US rules (19 CFR 122.49a(b)(1)(ii)(E)), before using an interactive APIS transmission system 'a carrier must subject its electronic transmission system to CBP testing, and CBP must certify' it. CBP keeps a Certified Vendor List for APIS Pre-Departure. Similar API/PNR connections (TSA Secure Flight, EU PNR, India, others) must be re-tested when the sending system changes. In mergers the FAA single operating certificate process runs alongside a PSS consolidation (Alaska/Hawaiian) but does not approve the PSS itself. Data-protection obligations (such as a GDPR DPIA) also apply. So: certification of the border-data interfaces, not approval of the core swap. Sources: https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/19/122.49a and https://www.cbp.gov/travel/travel-industry-personnel/advance-passenger-information-system

categories.regulator_note: Market infrastructure cores (exchanges, CCPs, CSDs) need a regulator's sign-off before cutover. SEBI suspended MCX's planned 3 Oct 2023 move to the TCS platform and only lifted the suspension after its Technical Advisory Committee approved it on 8 Oct 2023. MCX then went live on 16 Oct 2023. ASIC and the RBA supervise the ASX CHESS replacement. ASIC sued ASX over its CHESS statements, and the Federal Court ordered a A$20.5m penalty in 2026. OCC's move to Ovation runs through SEC and CFTC rule filings. Vietnam's Ministry of Finance and SSC tied the HOSE KRX go-live to stability and safety checks. At broker level, the regulator usually wants notice (outsourcing or technology-risk notifications, exchange or CCP connectivity re-certification and mock trading) rather than formal approval. Exchanges and clearing houses still have to certify every new back-office or front-end system that connects to them.

categories.regulator_note: Swapping a card processor or card management system is mostly a notification regime, not a licence approval, and it applies whenever the new platform is outsourced or offshored. Australia: APRA CPS 230 requires notice to APRA within 20 business days of entering into or materially changing an agreement for a service that supports a critical operation, and notice BEFORE any material offshoring arrangement (https://www.apra.gov.au/standards/cps-230). EU/UK: EBA Outsourcing Guidelines (EBA/GL/2019/02, para 59, also adopted by the Bank of England/PRA) require institutions to inform the competent authority in good time of planned outsourcing of critical or important functions. I saw this only in search results and did not open the guidelines text. Card-scheme (Visa/Mastercard) certification of the new platform is a further gate, but it comes from the schemes, not a regulator. Government programs need the agency itself to agree (Treasury Fiscal Service selected Fifth Third for Direct Express). I did not open MAS, RBI, OJK, SBV, BNM, BOT or BSP outsourcing rules, so 'true' for Asian markets is inferred, not verified.

categories.regulator_note: No regulator approves or must be notified before a contractor replaces its project-accounting ERP in any of the 11 regions. Rules apply to the outputs, not to the system choice. Examples: US certified payroll (Davis-Bacon WH-347), percentage-of-completion revenue recognition (ASC 606 / IFRS 15) checked by auditors, sureties' WIP reporting, and UK CIS returns. The nearest thing to oversight is US defence contracting. DFARS 252.242-7006 requires contractors to "establish and maintain an acceptable accounting system", and the Contracting Officer can flag material weaknesses after the fact. The clause has no prior-approval or notification step for a system change (https://www.acquisition.gov/dfars/252.242-7006-accounting-system-administration.). Cost Accounting Standards notices cover changes to cost accounting practices, not software. Listed contractors (Kier, Balfour Beatty, Interserve) disclosed ERP programmes only through capex and impairment reporting to investors.

categories.regulator_note: In most of the study regions, a core replacement must at least be reported to the regulator. Outright approval is rare. Indonesia: POJK 75/POJK.03/2016 Art. 25 requires a BPR or BPRS to report its IT-provider arrangement to OJK within 10 working days of the provider-run system going live. Late reports are fined Rp100,000 per day, and missing reports Rp5M (text opened at ojk.go.id). POJK 34/2025 replaces it and adds on-shore data-centre and DR rules. US: FDIC-supervised community and mutual banks must notify the FDIC within 30 days of a new service contract under Bank Service Company Act s.7 (12 CFR 304.3). Federally insured credit unions have no NCUA pre-approval step for a core change. Philippines: rural banks move under the BSP Rural Bank Strengthening Program (M-2026-042), which funds the change, and BSP outsourcing and IT-risk rules apply. India: PACS migrate under a government-mandated common ERP run by NABARD (Ministry of Cooperation). UCBs fall under RBI IT and outsourcing directions. Malaysia (Bank Rakyat, BNM-supervised under DFIA), Australia (APRA CPS 230 material service providers) and the EU (EBA outsourcing guidelines, notification of critical outsourcing) also require notification. Germany's Volks- and Raiffeisenbanken run on the group utility Atruvia, so a bank-level core change is effectively a group decision. Approval-type gates exist for government or apex programmes (India PACS, Philippine BSP subsidy). Elsewhere the requirement is notification, not approval. On that basis the flag is set to true.

categories.regulator_note: No regulator in these markets formally approves a core vendor in advance. But swapping or outsourcing the core sets off mandatory notice and supervisory review in each one. US: the Bank Service Company Act s.7(c) requires a bank to notify its federal regulator within 30 days of signing a contract for, or first receiving, third-party data processing such as posting deposits and computing interest (FDIC FIL-49-99). UK: under PRA SS2/21 firms must notify the PRA before they enter or significantly change a material outsourcing arrangement. A hosted core qualifies. The TSB 2018 migration ended in FCA and PRA fines totalling GBP48.65M (FCA Final Notice, 20 Dec 2022). EU: BaFin appointed a special representative at Deutsche Bank on 29 Sep 2023 over Postbank service disruptions after the Unity migration. For SG (MAS), IN (RBI), ID (OJK), MY (BNM), TH (BOT), PH (BSP) and AU (APRA CPS 230), I did not open the outsourcing and technology-risk notice rules in this pass. All of them require notice or consultation for material IT outsourcing, so a cutover is in practice a supervised event everywhere.

categories.regulator_note: No sector regulator has to approve or be notified before a court replaces its case management system. Courts are a self-governing branch, and the buyer is the judiciary itself or its justice ministry (the Judicial Council, the Administrative Office of the US Courts, HMCTS, the eCommittee and NIC, Mahkamah Agung). The real gates are funding and oversight. A legislature or cabinet must appropriate the money: India's Union Cabinet approved eCourts Phase III (Rs 7,210 crore), the California legislature and Judicial Council funded and then halted CCMS, and UK HM Treasury and the NAO scrutinise HMCTS business cases. Auditors review projects afterwards (CA State Auditor, NAO, NSW Audit Office). In the US, any system that exchanges data with criminal-history repositories, NCIC or DMVs must meet the FBI CJIS Security Policy. That is an ongoing compliance duty, not a pre-approval to replace the core system.

categories.regulator_note:
No health regulator approves a hospital's switch from one EHR or PAS to another in the study regions. The constraints work through funding and certification instead:
- US: CMS Promoting Interoperability requires ONC-certified EHR technology. That certifies the product, not the buyer's switch. Federal programs (VA EHRM, DoD MHS GENESIS) are overseen by Congress and GAO.
- UK, SG, MY, AU (state health) and VA: public buyers need a funded business case approved by the treasury, ministry or central agency. Examples are NHS England Frontline Digitisation funding, MOH and Synapxe for Singapore's NGEMR, Malaysia MOH and MCMC funding, and Queensland and NSW cabinet funding with audit-office scrutiny.
- ID: PMK 24/2022 requires every facility to run electronic records and integrate with SATUSEHAT. A replacement must keep that integration, but no approval is needed.
- AI documentation overlays can be regulated as medical devices. In the UK, Tortus registered with the MHRA. That rule applies to the overlay, not to replacing the core.
Data-protection rules (HIPAA, GDPR, NHS DSPT) apply to the migration, but none requires prior approval.

categories.regulator_note: No regulator approves or must be notified before a wholesale distributor replaces its ERP. Private distributors can switch whenever they choose. Three groups have indirect duties. (1) Pharmaceutical wholesalers must keep systems that comply with traceability and good-distribution-practice rules (US DSCSA, EU GDP with computerised-system validation), so a cutover needs validation and records continuity, but no pre-approval. (2) Listed distributors must keep SOX/ICFR IT general controls effective, and they disclose material ERP disruption to investors. Avnet, Ingram Micro, ScanSource and Grainger all did so in SEC filings or earnings releases. (3) Alcohol, tobacco and excise wholesalers must keep tax-ledger continuity. None of these is an approval gate.

categories.regulator_note: No regulator approves or must be told in advance when a manufacturer replaces its ERP. Three regimes add work around a cutover, but none is an approval gate. (1) Pharma, medical-device and food plants must validate computerised systems before go-live: US FDA 21 CFR Part 11 and the quality-system rules, and EU GMP Annex 11. That means validation evidence for inspectors, not prior approval. (2) US-listed companies must disclose material changes to internal control over financial reporting after the fact (SEC Item 308(c)). A bad cutover can produce a material weakness: Revlon's 2018 SAP launch did, per its 10-K and the class action. (3) US defence contractors have business systems, including the Material Management and Accounting System, that DCMA reviews under DFARS. A new ERP can trigger a re-review, but it does not need consent in advance. State-owned manufacturers such as India's SAIL are audited after the fact by the national audit office (CAG), not approved beforehand. I opened no primary regulator page for this note; it rests on general knowledge of these rules.

categories.regulator_note: In most sectors, replacing an EAM/CMMS (Maximo, SAP PM, HxGN/Octave Attune EAM, IFS) needs no regulator approval or notice. It is an internal IT decision. There are sector exceptions. (1) Aviation: under EASA Part-CAMO, the organisation's continuing-airworthiness record system must be described in its exposition (CAME section 1.1a), and the competent authority approves that exposition. A change outside the pre-agreed scope therefore needs approval (EASA CAME user guide, https://www.easa.europa.eu/en/downloads/136218/en). The FAA plays a similar role through an operator's CAMP manual. (2) Nuclear and other safety-related plants apply QA rules to software that holds safety-related maintenance records. (3) Regulated utilities and rail usually need the regulator to accept the cost for rate or price-control recovery, not to approve the swap itself. Examples are US state PUCs, and in the UK Ofgem/ORR, which reviewed Network Rail's ORBIS asset-information programme. Defence and public bodies face audit-office scrutiny (GAO, ANAO, Algemene Rekenkamer, Rigsrevisionen, CAG) rather than prior approval.

categories.regulator_note: No regulator approves a general ledger replacement at an ordinary company in any of the 11 regions. The constraint is the audit. The GL is the system of record behind audited statements, so the external auditor tests the migration and the controls around it (SOX/ICFR in the US, equivalent statutory audit rules elsewhere). A failed cutover can produce a material weakness or a qualified opinion. Birmingham City Council could not produce auditable accounts after its 2022 Oracle go-live. Two exceptions apply. (1) Regulated financial institutions. When a GL move is a material outsourcing or cloud arrangement, the supervisor must be notified: MAS outsourcing guidelines (SG), APRA CPS 230 material service providers (AU), and the EBA outsourcing guidelines for critical functions (EU). This is notification, not approval of the GL itself. (2) Public bodies. Government GLs (DEAMS, Coast Guard FSMS, HSE IFMS, Malaysia iGFMAS, Indonesia SAKTI) go through treasury or finance-ministry mandates and audit-office review rather than a licensing regulator. Indonesia made SAKTI mandatory for all work units by finance-ministry regulation (PMK).

categories.regulator_note: US: a state must get prior federal approval through an Advance Planning Document (APD) before buying eligibility or benefit system equipment or services with federal matching funds. This applies at $5M or more at the regular match, above $500K at the enhanced Medicaid match, and at $1M or more for a sole-source buy (45 CFR 95.611). CMS, ACF and FNS review these, and federal program offices sign off on Medicaid, SNAP and TANF integrated-eligibility replacements. State UI systems are funded by DOL grants and follow DOL conditions. Outside the US, the buyer is usually the national agency itself (DWP, Services Australia, CPF Board, EPFO, BPJS, VSS, SSS). So replacement is gated by Treasury, Cabinet or ministry business-case approval and audit-office scrutiny, not by a separate regulator. EU institutions must also keep their EESSI connection working through any core swap. Source: https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/95.611

categories.regulator_note: No sector regulator has to approve or be notified when a city, council or licensing board replaces its permitting or licensing system. The agency is itself the regulator, and replacements go through normal public procurement. Oversight bodies only apply to large state or national builds. Dutch national ICT projects over EUR 5M are reviewed by the Adviescollege ICT-toetsing (it reviewed DSO in Oct 2022), and the Omgevingswet start date needed the consent of both chambers of parliament. categories.regulator_note: Tax agencies are regulators themselves, so no sector regulator signs off on a core replacement the way a central bank does for core banking. Two outside checks still apply. (1) Notification. Any US federal, state or local agency handling Federal Tax Information must send the IRS Office of Safeguards a Cloud Computing Notification at least 45 days before FTI enters a new cloud environment (IRS Pub 1075; https://www.irs.gov/privacy-disclosure/cloud-computing-environment). Every state DOR moving its integrated tax system to a SaaS or cloud platform falls under this. (2) Funding and oversight approval, which is political, not regulatory. Congress funds IRS modernization: about $6bn in BSM funding FY1998-2024, and CADE 2 successor projects were suspended in May 2024 (CRS IF12525). State legislatures fund state DOR projects; North Carolina's ITS replacement is funded at $25m a year under S.L. 2023-134 and reports to legislative committees twice a year. HMRC had to justify the single-source GBP 275m SAP award (The Register). Audit offices review delivery: Rigsrevisionen on Denmark's EFI, the Bundesrechnungshof and the state audit offices on Germany's KONSENS, the IGT and ANAO on the ATO, and the NAO on HMRC's MTD. Approval here means a budget or business case, not a licence.

categories.regulator_note: In most of the study's regions a regulator must be told before a core system moves to a vendor. Formal approval of the claims system itself is not required. EU: DORA Art. 28(3) requires insurers to inform the competent authority in a timely manner of any planned ICT contract supporting critical or important functions, which covers a core claims platform or SaaS (https://www.digital-operational-resilience-act.com/Article_28.html). UK: PRA SS2/21 applies to Solvency II insurers, Lloyd's and managing agents. It expects prior notification before entering or significantly changing a material outsourcing, such as a hosted claims core. AU: APRA CPS 230 requires notice within 20 business days of entering or materially changing an arrangement that supports a critical operation, and prior notice for material offshoring (https://www.apra.gov.au/standards/cps-230). SG, IN and ID run similar outsourcing and IT-risk regimes (MAS outsourcing guidelines, IRDAI outsourcing regulations, OJK IT-risk rules); I did not open these primary texts for this pass. US: there is no federal or state pre-approval for a carrier changing its claims system. Market-conduct exams and claims-handling rules apply after the fact. Public schemes (state funds, FEMA NFIP, icare, NHS Resolution) instead face legislative or treasury oversight of the IT budget. Washington L&I's project, for example, files quarterly proviso reports to the Legislature and was suspended by state oversight in Aug 2025.

categories.regulator_note:
No region requires a regulator to approve the core-system choice itself. The duty comes from outsourcing and cloud rules, which apply because most replacements now move to vendor SaaS or offshore delivery. Replacing an in-house core on-premises usually triggers no filing, and in the US no prior approval is needed (state examiners review IT afterwards).
- EU: Solvency II Art. 49(3) requires insurers to notify the supervisor before outsourcing critical or important functions. EIOPA's cloud outsourcing guidelines apply this to cloud providers (eiopa.europa.eu, EIOPA-BoS-20-002).
- AU: APRA CPS 230 requires notice within 20 business days of entering or materially changing an arrangement with a material service provider for a critical operation. Material offshoring needs notice beforehand (apra.gov.au/standards/cps-230).
- UK (PRA SS2/21) and SG (MAS outsourcing guidelines): notification regimes for material outsourcing. Not re-opened in this pass.
- ID (OJK), TH (OIC), MY (BNM), IN (IRDAI): similar outsourcing and data-location rules. Not re-opened in this pass.

categories.regulator_note: No regulator approves or must be told in advance when a clinical lab replaces its LIS in the regions studied. The lab carries the burden through validation. In the US, CLIA and the CAP checklists require the LIS to be validated at installation and after every change. CAP GEN.48500 also requires a procedure to check that results reach the patient report accurately before go-live and every 2 years after. ISO 15189 accreditation bodies in the UK, EU, AU and Asia (UKAS, NATA, NABL, SAC, etc.) set the same expectation. The exception is blood bank modules. FDA classes blood establishment computer software as a Class II device cleared through 510(k), and about 220 had been cleared by 2015. A US blood bank that changes systems must therefore move to an FDA-cleared product and run a BECS validation programme. Public buyers add a de facto approval layer. NHS England networks need NHSE/I sign-off of their LIMS business cases: Kent and Medway's OBC was approved in May 2021 and its FBC in Feb 2022. Australian state projects face auditor-general review (PathWest).

workflows.workflow: Specimen receipt, requisition intake and order entry
workflows.description: Staff receive specimens with paper, faxed or electronic requisitions. They match tubes to orders, key patient, test and insurance data into the LIS, apply barcode labels, and chase problem specimens (missing orders, mislabels) with collection sites. AI requisition OCR (MarginLogic, Onymos, CrelioHealth) can feed clean orders into the existing LIS without replacing it.

occupations.title: Data Entry Keyers

Compile, sort, and verify the accuracy of data before it is entered.
Compare data with source documents, or re-enter data in verification format to detect errors.
Locate and correct data entry errors, or report them to supervisors.

occupations.title: Cytotechnologists

workflows.workflow: Result review, autoverification, release and critical-value calls
workflows.description: Technologists review analyzer and manual results, apply delta and range checks, order repeats or dilutions, enter non-interfaced results (microscopy, micro plates), then verify and release them to the EHR. They phone critical values and document read-back in the LIS. The autoverification rules and the result of record live in the LIS, so moving this workflow means replacing the core.

occupations.title: Medical and Clinical Laboratory Technologists

Enter data from analysis of medical tests or clinical results into computer for storage.
Provide technical information about test results to physicians, family members, or researchers.
Cultivate, isolate, or assist in identifying microbial organisms or perform various tests on these microorganisms.

occupations.title: Medical and Clinical Laboratory Technicians
onet_tasks: Conduct chemical analyses of body fluids, such as blood or urine, using microscope or automatic analyzer to detect abnormalities or diseases and enter findings into computer.
Analyze and record test data to issue reports that use charts, graphs, or narratives.
Analyze the results of tests or experiments to ensure conformity to specifications, using special mechanical or electrical devices.

workflows.workflow: Quality control, calibration and instrument maintenance
workflows.description: Staff run and record daily QC and calibrations, review Levey-Jennings charts, document corrective actions, perform preventive maintenance, and log instrument downtime. Most of this sits in middleware and QC software (Data Innovations, Bio-Rad Unity) next to the LIS, so it can change without replacing the core.

occupations.title: Medical and Clinical Laboratory Technologists
onet_tasks: Establish or monitor quality assurance programs or activities to ensure the accuracy of laboratory results.
Operate, calibrate, or maintain equipment used in quantitative or qualitative analysis, such as spectrophotometers, calorimeters, flame photometers, or computer-controlled analyzers.
Set up, clean, and maintain laboratory equipment.

occupations.title: Medical and Clinical Laboratory Technicians

Set up, maintain, calibrate, clean, and test sterility of medical laboratory equipment.

occupations.title: Histotechnologists

Resolve problems with laboratory equipment and instruments, such as microscopes, mass spectrometers, microtomes, immunostainers, tissue processors, embedding centers, and water baths.

workflows.workflow: Anatomic pathology case tracking, diagnosis and report sign-out
workflows.description: Histology and cytology staff track blocks and slides and assemble cases. Pathologists examine slides, dictate or type reports, and sign them out, and secretaries transcribe and route the reports. AI-native entrants (elea, Voquill) target this workflow with voice-driven reporting and aim to replace the AP LIS outright. Digital pathology overlays (Proscia, PathAI, Techcyte) sit beside it.

occupations.title: Physicians, Pathologists

Examine microscopic samples to identify diseases or other abnormalities.
Communicate pathologic findings to surgeons or other physicians.

occupations.title: Histotechnologists
onet_tasks: Compile materials for distribution to pathologists, such as surgical working drafts, requisitions, and slides.
Examine slides under microscopes to ensure tissue preparation meets laboratory requirements.

occupations.title: Cytotechnologists
onet_tasks: Submit slides with abnormal cell structures to pathologists for further examination.
Provide patient clinical data or microscopic findings to assist pathologists in the preparation of pathology reports.

occupations.title: Medical Secretaries and Administrative Assistants

Receive and route messages or documents, such as laboratory results, to appropriate staff.

workflows.workflow: Send-out testing, CPT coding and lab billing
workflows.description: Staff package send-out tests for reference labs, build manifests, and re-key returned results. They also assign CPT/ICD codes, check billing data and work denials, usually in a separate lab RCM system interfaced to the LIS. Interface-level automation and AI coding can replace this without touching the LIS of record.

categories.regulator_note: Most land registries are government bodies, so the registry is usually its own regulator. Replacing the core register still needs outside sign-off in three ways. (1) Statute often fixes the register's form, so a new system needs new law. Telangana's Bhu Bharati came with the Bhu Bharati (Record of Rights in Land) Act 2024 (Act 1 of 2025), Malaysia amended the National Land Code for SPTB, and Queensland's ATS was set up under the Land Title Act 1994. (2) Where the registry is run under a concession, a regulator oversees the operator's technology. In NSW, the Office of the Registrar General reviews the operator's technology roadmaps and meets it quarterly through an IT sub-committee (NSW Audit Office, Feb 2025). The ORG does not formally approve each IT change. (3) Donor- or audit-supervised programmes need lender or auditor review: World Bank ICRs for Vietnam VILG, COA special audits for the Philippines LTCP, and Austria's Rechnungshof for GDB-NEU. US county recorders are the exception. A county board approves the contract (for example DuPage, Feb 2026, and Spokane, 2026), and no state regulator approves the system. Source: https://www.audit.nsw.gov.au/our-work/reports/regulation-of-the-land-titles-registry

categories.regulator_note: No regulator gives formal pre-approval for a new loan system as such. Banks in most of the 11 regions must still notify their supervisor, and some must notify before they move. US: under the Bank Service Company Act, 12 U.S.C. 1867(c), an insured bank must notify its federal banking agency within 30 days of contracting a third-party technology servicer. Nonbank mortgage servicers have no system-change notice in Fannie Mae's A4-1-03, but servicing transfers need GSE approval (Form 629). State settlements can force a system change: Ocwen's multistate settlements required it to leave REALServicing. AU: APRA CPS 230 requires notice within 20 business days of entering a material service-provider arrangement for a critical operation, and prior notice for material offshoring. MY: BNM RMiT requires consulting the Bank before a bank first puts a critical system on public cloud, and notifying it after that. SG: MAS Notice 658 (effective Dec 2024) governs material outsourcing, and MAS can require pre-notification. UK: the PRA and FCA fined TSB GBP 48.65M over its 2018 platform migration, which included mortgages, so supervisors expect advance engagement. In the euro area, BaFin appointed a special monitor after Deutsche Bank's 2023 Postbank migration. Sources: law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/12/1867, apra.gov.au/standards/cps-230, bankofengland.co.uk TSB news release (Dec 2022), selling-guide.fanniemae.com A4-1-03.

workflows.workflow: Application intake and borrower origination contact
workflows.description: A loan officer or interviewer takes the application by phone, branch or web, keys it into the LOS, pulls credit, quotes rates and answers borrower questions. Voice and point-of-sale AI agents (Sela, Tidalwave) work in front of the LOS and do not replace it.

occupations.title: Loan Officers
onet_tasks: Meet with applicants to obtain information for loan applications and to answer questions about the process.
Explain to customers the different types of loans and credit options that are available, as well as the terms of those services.
Obtain and compile copies of loan applicants' credit histories, corporate financial statements, and other financial information.
Contact applicants or creditors to resolve questions about applications or to assist with completion of paperwork.

occupations.title: Loan Interviewers and Clerks
onet_tasks: Interview loan applicants to obtain personal and financial data and to assist in completing applications.
Answer questions and advise customers regarding loans and transactions.
Contact customers by mail, telephone, or in person concerning acceptance or rejection of applications.
Present loan and repayment schedules to customers.

workflows.workflow: Document processing, verification and underwriting
workflows.description: Processors collect and index borrower documents, verify employment and third-party items, and clear conditions. Underwriters and credit analysts assess income, DTI, credit and collateral, then approve, suspend or decline. AI document and underwriting agents feed the existing LOS.

occupations.title: Credit Analysts
onet_tasks: Analyze credit data and financial statements to determine the degree of risk involved in extending credit or lending money.
Complete loan applications, including credit analyses and summaries of loan requests, and submit to loan committees for approval.
Generate financial ratios, using computer programs, to evaluate customers' financial status.
Prepare reports that include the degree of risk involved in extending credit or lending money.

occupations.title: Loan Officers
onet_tasks: Analyze applicants' financial status, credit, and property evaluations to determine feasibility of granting loans.
Approve loans within specified limits, and refer loan applications outside those limits to management for approval.
Submit applications to credit analysts for verification and recommendation.
Confer with underwriters to resolve mortgage application problems.

occupations.title: Loan Interviewers and Clerks
onet_tasks: Contact credit bureaus, employers, and other sources to check applicants' credit and personal references.
Submit loan applications with recommendation for underwriting approval.
Check value of customer collateral to be held as loan security.
Verify and examine information and accuracy of loan application and closing documents.

workflows.workflow: Closing, funding, post-closing and boarding to servicing
workflows.description: Closers prepare disclosures and loan documents, coordinate with title and settlement agents, and fund the loan. Post-closing staff check file completeness and ship files to investors. Boarding staff map loan terms from the LOS into the servicing system. All of this happens inside the LOS system of record, so taking it over means replacing the LOS (Fuse, Lama AI).

occupations.title: Loan Interviewers and Clerks
onet_tasks: Prepare and type loan applications, closing documents, legal documents, letters, forms, government notices, and checks, using computers.
Assemble and compile documents for loan closings, such as title abstracts, insurance forms, loan forms, and tax receipts.
Schedule and conduct closings of mortgage transactions.
Record applications for loan and credit, loan information, and disbursements of funds, using computers.
File and maintain loan records.

occupations.title: Title Examiners, Abstractors, and Searchers
onet_tasks: Retrieve and examine real estate closing files for accuracy and to ensure that information included is recorded and executed according to regulations.
Prepare real estate closing statements, using knowledge and expertise in real estate procedures.
Confer with realtors, lending institution personnel, buyers, sellers, contractors, surveyors, and courthouse personnel to exchange title-related information or to resolve problems.

occupations.title: Loan Officers
onet_tasks: Review loan agreements to ensure that they are complete and accurate according to policy.
Review and update credit and loan files.

workflows.workflow: Payment processing, custodial reconciliation and escrow administration
workflows.description: Servicing staff post borrower payments, research exceptions and reconcile custodial accounts. They pay property taxes and insurance from escrow and run annual escrow analyses. All of this runs as batch processing on the servicing core (e.g. ICE MSP), so replacing the workflow means replacing the core (ValonOS, Sagent Dara).

occupations.title: Bookkeeping, Accounting, and Auditing Clerks
onet_tasks: Receive, record, and bank cash, checks, and vouchers.
Reconcile or note and report discrepancies found in records.
Calculate and prepare checks for utilities, taxes, and other payments.
Monitor status of loans and accounts to ensure that payments are up to date.
Reconcile records of bank transactions.

occupations.title: Loan Interviewers and Clerks
onet_tasks: Accept payment on accounts.
Calculate, review, and correct errors on interest, principal, payment, and closing costs, using computers or calculators.
Order property insurance or mortgage insurance policies to ensure protection against loss on mortgaged property.
Review customer accounts to determine whether payments are made on time and that other loan terms are being followed.

workflows.workflow: Borrower servicing calls and inquiries
workflows.description: Reps handle calls about payoff quotes, statements, payments and escrow, and record each interaction in the servicing system. Voice and text AI agents (Kastle) answer these calls and write back to the existing core.

occupations.title: Customer Service Representatives
onet_tasks: Confer with customers by telephone or in person to provide information about products or services, take or enter orders, cancel accounts, or obtain details of complaints.
Keep records of customer interactions or transactions, recording details of inquiries, complaints, or comments, as well as actions taken.
Determine charges for services requested, collect deposits or payments, or arrange for billing.
Complete contract forms, prepare change of address records, or issue service discontinuance orders, using computers.
Refer unresolved customer grievances to designated departments for further investigation.

categories.regulator_note: No regulator approves a mainframe or COBOL replacement as such in this cross-industry category. The duty depends on the sector. Regulated banks and insurers must notify their supervisor before material IT outsourcing or cloud moves: the PRA under SS2/21, APRA under CPS 230, MAS under its outsourcing and Technology Risk Management guidelines, EU banks under the EBA outsourcing guidelines, and the RBI, BNM, OJK, BSP and BOT under their IT and outsourcing rules. In practice that makes core migrations at banks and insurers notifiable. The TSB case shows supervisors (FCA and PRA) can fine a bank after a migration fails (GBP 48.65M in 2022). Government agencies face oversight from auditors and legislatures (GAO, ANAO, state auditors, the Bundesrechnungshof), not prior approval. Non-financial firms (retail, logistics, telco) generally need no approval.

categories.regulator_note: No regulator in the 11 regions has to approve a provider replacing its billing or revenue cycle system. The checks are about connectivity and procurement. In the US, a provider that changes billing software or clearinghouse updates its EDI enrollment and submitter set-up with each payer and Medicare contractor and tests claim files. That is a notification and test step, not an approval. Public buyers face procurement and legislative oversight instead. VA's Oracle Health program reports to congressional committees and GAO. The NSW SDPR and Queensland HBCIS projects were reviewed by state audit offices. Singapore's NGEMR and National Billing System are run by MOH and Synapxe directly. In Indonesia, India, Thailand, Vietnam and the Philippines, a hospital's HIS must keep bridging to the national payer claim systems (BPJS V-Claim/E-Klaim, PM-JAY/NHCX, NHSO e-Claim, the VSS insurance gateway, PhilHealth eClaims) or claims stop flowing. That is an integration requirement, not prior approval. I did not open primary sources for the payer-bridging rules, so treat that part as background.

categories.regulator_note: US: Ginnie Mae MBS Guide Ch. 21 Part 7 says an issuer moving servicing to a subservicer, in-house from a subservicer, between subservicers, or 'even a transfer to an in-house servicing platform' must notify Ginnie Mae and get its prior written approval. Any change to an in-house servicing platform that could affect reported data also needs RFS (Reporting and Feedback System) testing. Ginnie Mae is a federal guarantor inside HUD, not a bank regulator. State regulators can also dictate system moves. Ocwen's 2017-2018 multistate settlements required a plan of action and milestones for leaving REALServicing and barred new loans on that system. NY DFS required all New York loans off REALServicing by April 30 2020. UK: no formal pre-approval for a core swap was found, but the FCA and PRA supervise migrations and fined TSB £48.65m over its 2018 platform migration. In the EU, AU and Asia, bank system replacements fall under outsourcing and operational-resilience notification regimes. Those regimes were not verified for this category.

categories.regulator_note: In none of the 11 regions does a regulator approve, or need notice of, an employer's switch to a new payroll or HR system of record. The constraints work at three other levels. (1) The software vendor must be certified for statutory reporting. Examples: HMRC RTI-recognised payroll software in the UK, ATO Single Touch Payroll-enabled software in Australia, and local tax and social-security formats (PPh 21 and BPJS in Indonesia, EPF and ESI in India, CPF in Singapore, SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG in the Philippines). (2) Public-sector replacements go through budget and IT oversight. Examples: California's CSPS through the Legislature and the Department of Technology, and NHS ESR through national procurement. (3) For regulated financial firms, outsourcing payroll to a SaaS or cloud provider can trigger outsourcing notifications (for example the EBA outsourcing guidelines or MAS outsourcing guidelines), but that applies to a few firms and not to the category. Practical gating comes from parallel runs, tax-year boundaries and union or works-council consultation. In Germany, the works council has co-determination rights over HR IT systems. No regulator gate applies.

categories.regulator_note: The answer depends on the region. AU: APRA CPS 230 has been in force since 1 Jul 2025, with pre-existing contracts given until 1 Jul 2026. RSE licensees must notify APRA within 20 business days of entering into or materially changing a material service provider arrangement, which includes fund administrators. Offshoring needs prior notification. APRA put licence conditions on HESTA in Dec 2025 after its admin transition (https://www.apra.gov.au/operational-risk-management, https://www.apra.gov.au/news-and-publications/apra-imposes-additional-licence-conditions-hesta). EU: IORP II requires notifying the national competent authority before outsourcing key functions or activities; this was not re-verified in this pass. UK: TPR does not approve admin system changes. Government-run schemes still go through sponsor approval and NAO/PAC scrutiny, as with the Civil Service Pension Scheme move to Capita. US: no regulator approves a private 401(k) recordkeeper switch (ERISA fiduciary duty only). Public plans need legislative budget approval, for example Nevada PERS PARIS and Washington DRS CORE:PAM. IN, SG, MY, ID, VN, PH and TH: the national provident or social security fund is itself a state body, so any core change needs ministry or board approval. EPFO's CITES 2.01, for example, was approved by its Central Board of Trustees and built by C-DAC.

categories.regulator_note: No port or maritime regulator in the 11 regions approves or must be notified of a TOS replacement. A TOS is an operator's internal system. The real gates are governance and interfaces. Public port authorities need board approval and must follow public procurement rules: SC Ports' board approved an $11.9M N4 infrastructure contract in Dec 2011, Port Authority of Guam ran RFI PAG/RFI-023-001 (2023) and then RFP-PAG-025-001 (closed 27 Oct 2025), and Indian major ports buy through GeM or tender. Landlord concessions can also need consent from the port authority or ministry. The cutover itself has to re-test customs and port-community EDI links (for example customs holds and releases, ICEGATE in India, PCS links such as Felixstowe's MCP and 1-Stop in AU) and gate access-control integrations that sit under ISPS/MTSA facility security plans. No source shows a formal approval step for any of these. Treat them as interface re-certification, not regulatory approval.

Review logistics performance with customers against targets, benchmarks, and service agreements.
Direct team activities, establishing task priorities, scheduling and tracking work assignments, providing guidance, and ensuring the availability of resources.

occupations.title: Production, Planning, and Expediting Clerks

Distribute production schedules or work orders to departments.
Compile information, such as production rates and progress, materials inventories, materials used, or customer information, so that status reports can be completed.

workflows.workflow: Yard allocation and housekeeping planning

occupations.title: Transportation, Storage, and Distribution Managers

categories.regulator_note: No regulator has to approve or be notified before a company or public body replaces its purchasing or payables system. This differs from core banking, insurance policy admin and EHR. The constraints sit next to the replacement decision. US-listed companies have to keep SOX internal controls over financial reporting working through the cutover, and Revlon's 2018 SAP go-live ended in a disclosed material weakness. Public bodies have to buy the replacement under their own procurement law (UK councils, Ireland's HSE, Australian Defence under the Commonwealth Procurement Rules) and answer to auditors-general afterwards; see the UK council, Irish C&AG, ANAO, Malaysian Auditor-General and GAO cases. A new AP system also has to plug into government e-invoicing and tax rails where they exist, such as India's GST e-invoice portal, Malaysia's LHDN MyInvois, Peppol-based InvoiceNow in Singapore and Australia, and EU e-invoicing mandates. These are integration and compliance duties, not approval gates.

categories.regulator_note: In most study regions (US, UK, SG, AU, MY, IN), no sector regulator has to approve a change of POS or merchandising system before it happens. The constraints that do exist come from tax authorities and apply to the fiscal POS layer only, never to merchandising. Philippines: under RR 11-2004, RMO 10-2005 and RR 16-2024, the BIR requires the POS/CRM software to be accredited and each machine to be registered (Permit to Use, now an acknowledgement certificate) before it can issue receipts. A replacement POS in PH therefore needs prior BIR clearance. Germany: since 1 Jan 2025, section 146a(4) AO requires each electronic cash system to be reported to the tax office within one month of acquisition or decommissioning (systems bought before 1 Jul 2025 had to be reported by 31 Jul 2025). That is a notice after the fact, not an approval. Other EU fiscal-printer regimes (e.g. IT, PL) and TH Revenue Department rules on POS tax invoices may add certification steps; these were not verified here. PCI DSS and EMV payment re-certification apply everywhere but come from card schemes, not regulators. Sources opened: finanzamt.hessen.de (Mitteilungspflicht fuer Kassensysteme) and respicio.ph (BIR POS registration requirements).

categories.regulator_note: None of the 11 regions requires a regulator to approve, or be notified of, a student information system replacement. The constraint is that statutory data returns must keep flowing through the cutover. Those returns include IPEDS and Title IV reporting in the US, the HESA Data Futures/OfS and DfE school census returns in the UK, PDDikti Feeder in Indonesia, AISHE in India, CHED in the Philippines and TEQSA in Australia. Data protection rules (GDPR/UK GDPR DPIAs, PDPA in SG/MY/TH, FERPA in the US) also apply. Public buyers face their own government IT and budget oversight. For example, Washington's ctcLink needed OCIO gated-funding approvals (Gate 4a/4b, 2019), and NSW Treasury oversaw LMBR. These are funding and oversight gates, not sign-off from an education regulator.

categories.regulator_note: None of the 11 regions makes an operator get regulator sign-off before it replaces its BSS or billing system, so this is false. Three rules come close. (1) UK: Ofcom General Condition C3 requires providers above a turnover threshold to have their Total Metering and Billing System approved by a third-party Approval Body that Ofcom recognises. The threshold is £40m in older Ofcom documents and £55m in later ones; we did not confirm the current figure. A new billing platform has to be brought back into that approval. This is a certification after the fact, not permission to switch (ofcom.org.uk Metering and Billing Scheme). (2) India: under the TRAI Quality of Service (Code of Practice for Metering and Billing Accuracy) Regulations 2006, every access provider must have its metering and billing system audited each year by a TRAI-empanelled auditor and file the certificate by 30 June. This is an annual audit, not prior approval. (3) US: state utility commissions oversaw systems cutovers that were tied to merger conditions. Examples are the Vermont PSB and the NH/ME commissions for FairPoint in 2009 (Vermont PSB Docket 7540), plus later scrutiny of Frontier's 2016 CTF flash cut. This is merger-specific, not a general rule. Regulators step in after a migration fails. Ofcom fined Vodafone UK £4.6m in 2016 for billing failures caused by its migration.

categories.regulator_note: No regulator I found approves a trade finance engine swap as such. Notice or consultation is required, though, when the new system is outsourced, offshore or in the cloud, and the SaaS and hosted moves (CGI Trade360, DOKA-NG private cloud, BNI's central Jakarta hub) fall in that case. Australia: under APRA CPS 230 a bank must notify APRA within 20 business days of entering or materially changing an agreement for a service it relies on for a critical operation, and before entering a material offshoring arrangement (https://www.apra.gov.au/standards/cps-230). Malaysia: under the BNM RMiT update (cloud rules in force 1 June 2024 for most institutions), a bank must consult BNM before its first public-cloud adoption for critical systems and notify BNM of each later one (https://www.mondaq.com/new-technology/1399776/updated-policy-document-on-risk-management-in-technology-rmit-additional-requirements-relating-to-management-of-cloud-technology-risks). I did not open sources for MAS outsourcing, OJK offshore-system placement, RBI IT outsourcing or the EU and UK outsourcing regimes. A like-for-like on-premise replacement may need no regulator notice.

categories.regulator_note: No regulator in the 11 regions pre-approves a CIS swap as such. Oversight comes before the swap through cost recovery and rule waivers, and after it through enforcement. US: state commissions review CIS spending for prudence in rate cases. Duke Energy put its $900M Customer Connect (SAP) programme into its 2019 Indiana rate case. In Ohio, PUCO had to grant rule waivers before installation in Jan 2022, then proposed a $1.45M fine and ordered a third-party audit after more than 106,000 billing errors. UK: Ofgem does not approve migrations but enforces billing standards afterwards. npower reported SAP problems to Ofgem in Dec 2012 and paid £26M in redress in 2015. Australia (AER) and the EU: no approval step; regulated billing rules still apply. Asia: in VN, ID, TH and MY the billing core sits inside a state utility (EVN, PLN, PEA/MEA, TNB), so the decision is a state-enterprise or ministry matter, not a licensing approval. In practice, a regulated utility in a rate-case jurisdiction usually discloses the project to its regulator before go-live because it wants the cost recovered.

categories.regulator_note: No regulator approves or must be told before a company swaps its WMS. Firms and agencies replaced their WMS in every case found here (DLA, AAFES, Sainsbury's, ASOS, Myer, FCI) without any regulator signing off first. There are indirect obligations, though. Pharma and medical-device distributors must validate a new computerised system under GxP and Good Distribution Practice rules. Customs-bonded and free-trade-zone warehouses must keep inventory records that customs will accept, such as US CBP bonded-warehouse rules, Singapore licensed warehouses and Indian customs bonded warehouses. Government buyers need an internal authority to operate; DLA, for example, phased its rollout site by site over 2018 to 2026. These are validation and audit duties after the fact, not prior approval. In India, the Warehousing Development and Regulatory Authority (WDRA) registers warehouses but does not approve their software.

categories.regulator_note: Rules differ by buyer type. Bank-owned wealth, trust and private-banking units must notify their regulator. They usually do not need formal approval, unless the system is outsourced to an offshore provider or the cloud. US banks and trust companies must tell their federal regulator about a new third-party service relationship within 30 days of signing (Bank Service Company Act, 12 USC 1867(c)), and examiners then review it. UK firms must notify the FCA before entering into, or significantly changing, a material outsourcing arrangement (SUP 15.3.8G), and a move to Avaloq SaaS or FNZ counts. Singapore banks fall under MAS Notice 658 on outsourced relevant services (effective 11 Dec 2024), and EU banks under the EBA outsourcing guidelines. APRA (CPS 230) and BSP apply similar regimes. SEC- and state-registered RIAs and family offices need no regulator sign-off to change portfolio accounting systems. They still carry books-and-records and custody-rule duties, so conversions must preserve history. Sources opened: handbook.fca.org.uk SUP 15.3; uscode.house.gov 12 USC 1867; mas.gov.sg Notice 658.

occupations.title: Bookkeeping, Accounting, and Auditing Clerks
onet_tasks: Reconcile or note and report discrepancies found in records.
Check figures, postings, and documents for correct entry, mathematical accuracy, and proper codes.
Compare computer printouts to manually maintained journals to determine if they match.
Debit, credit, and total accounts on computer spreadsheets and databases, using specialized accounting software.

occupations.title: Accountants and Auditors
onet_tasks: Review accounts for discrepancies and reconcile differences.
Inspect cash on hand, notes receivable and payable, negotiable securities, and canceled checks to confirm records are accurate.
Prepare, examine, or analyze accounting records, financial statements, or other financial reports to assess accuracy, completeness, and conformance to reporting and procedural standards.

workflows.workflow: Corporate actions, security pricing and cost basis
workflows.description: Staff process dividends, splits, mergers and voluntary elections. They fix the tax lots and cost basis these change, validate vendor prices and manually price illiquid holdings. All of this happens in the accounting engine's security master and lot records.

occupations.title: Brokerage Clerks
onet_tasks: Document security transactions, such as purchases, sales, conversions, redemptions, or payments, using computers, accounting ledgers, or certificate records.
Verify ownership and transaction information and dividend distribution instructions to ensure conformance with governmental regulations, using stock records and reports.
Compute total holdings, dividends, interest, transfer taxes, brokerage fees, or commissions and allocate appropriate payments to customers.
Monitor daily stock prices and compute fluctuations to determine the need for additional collateral to secure loans.

occupations.title: Bookkeeping, Accounting, and Auditing Clerks
onet_tasks: Perform financial calculations, such as amounts due, interest charges, balances, discounts, equity, and principal.
Classify, record, and summarize numerical and financial data to compile and keep financial records, using journals and ledgers or computers.

occupations.title: Financial and Investment Analysts
onet_tasks: Interpret data on price, yield, stability, future investment-risk trends, economic influences, and other factors affecting investment programs.
Evaluate and compare the relative quality of various securities in a given industry.

workflows.workflow: Performance measurement and client reporting
workflows.description: Reporting teams calculate returns, check holdings and performance for errors, and assemble quarterly client report packages. Reports are often built with REPLANG on Axys/APX or from data extracts, and overlays such as Addepar or Masttro can replace this step without touching the book of record.

occupations.title: Financial and Investment Analysts
onet_tasks: Draw charts and graphs, using computer spreadsheets, to illustrate technical reports.
Create client presentations of plan details.
Present oral or written reports on general economic trends, individual corporations, and entire industries.

occupations.title: Personal Financial Advisors
onet_tasks: Prepare or interpret for clients information, such as investment performance reports, financial document summaries, or income projections.

occupations.title: Bookkeeping, Accounting, and Auditing Clerks
onet_tasks: Compile statistical, financial, accounting, or auditing reports and tables pertaining to such matters as cash receipts, expenditures, accounts payable and receivable, and profits and losses.

occupations.title: Brokerage Clerks
onet_tasks: Prepare reports summarizing daily transactions and earnings for individual customer accounts.

workflows.workflow: Client review, planning and rebalancing
workflows.description: Advisors and portfolio managers prepare for and hold client reviews, document meetings, check model drift and cash needs, and generate and submit rebalancing trades. AI meeting and planning tools (Jump, Zocks, Nevis, Saturn) sit on top of the CRM and accounting data here.

occupations.title: Personal Financial Advisors
onet_tasks: Review clients' accounts and plans regularly to determine whether life changes, economic changes, environmental concerns, or financial performance indicate a need for plan reassessment.
Interview clients to determine their current income, expenses, insurance coverage, tax status, financial objectives, risk tolerance, or other information needed to develop a financial plan.
Manage client portfolios, keeping client plans up-to-date.
Answer clients' questions about the purposes and details of financial plans and strategies.
Contact clients periodically to determine any changes in their financial status.

occupations.title: Securities, Commodities, and Financial Services Sales Agents
onet_tasks: Complete sales order tickets and submit for processing of client-requested transactions.
Review all securities transactions to ensure accuracy of information and conformance to governing agency regulations.
Discuss financial options with clients and keep them informed about transactions.

workflows.workflow: Alternatives and private-fund data capture
workflows.description: Analysts collect capital calls, distributions, NAV statements and K-1s from GP portals and email PDFs, then key them into the accounting system. Document-extraction overlays (Canoe, Arch) feed clean data into the core instead of replacing it.

occupations.title: Data Entry Keyers
onet_tasks: Read source documents such as canceled checks, sales reports, or bills, and enter data in specific data fields or onto tapes or disks for subsequent entry, using keyboards or scanners.
Compare data with source documents, or re-enter data in verification format to detect errors.
Compile, sort, and verify the accuracy of data before it is entered.
Locate and correct data entry errors, or report them to supervisors.

occupations.title: Bookkeeping, Accounting, and Auditing Clerks
onet_tasks: Code documents according to company procedures.
Transfer details from separate journals to general ledgers or data processing sheets.

occupations.title: Accountants and Auditors
onet_tasks: Review data about material assets, net worth, liabilities, capital stock, surplus, income, or expenditures.

workflows.workflow: Account onboarding, money movement and fee billing
workflows.description: Staff collect account paperwork, initiate ACATS and other transfers, set up accounts and fee schedules, and process withdrawals and journals with callback checks. They also calculate AUM-based fees and produce invoices or custodian debit files.

occupations.title: New Accounts Clerks
onet_tasks: Compile information about new accounts, enter account information into computers, and file related forms or other documents.
Interview customers to obtain information needed for opening accounts or renting safe-deposit boxes.
Investigate and correct errors upon customers' request, according to customer and bank records.

occupations.title: Brokerage Clerks
onet_tasks: Prepare forms, such as receipts, withdrawal orders, transmittal papers, or transfer confirmations, based on transaction requests from stockholders.
Schedule and coordinate transfer and delivery of security certificates between companies, departments, and customers.

occupations.title: Billing and Posting Clerks
onet_tasks: Verify accuracy of billing data and revise any errors.
Prepare itemized statements, bills, or invoices and record amounts due for items purchased or services rendered.
Resolve discrepancies in accounting records.

occupations.title: Personal Financial Advisors
onet_tasks: Open accounts for clients, and disburse funds from accounts to creditors as agent for clients.
